glosses: critical (expressing criticism, pertaining to criticism or critique)
ernaar geneigd zijn iets te beoordelen (en dus vaak af te keuren)

examples.text: Het islamitische Haga Lyceum probeerde de publicatie van het uiterst kritische inspectierapport voor de zomer al te voorkomen, maar ook toen ving de school bot.

Toch fijn dat enkelen die vooraf zo fel en kritisch waren geweest, mij na afloop van de tocht een persoonlijk bericht stuurden om te zeggen hoe mooi ze het vonden dat ik mijn droom achterna was gegaan.

glosses: op het punt van de ene toestand over te gaan in de andere
onder zulke omstandigheden dat er meer neutronen geproduceerd dan geabsorbeerd worden, waardoor een nucleaire kettingreactie op gang kan komen.

translations.source_sense_description: ernaar geneigd vraagtekens te plaatsen achter iets

glosses: bedrohlich, entscheidend

examples.text: Die kritische Masse für eine Kernspaltung von Uran-235 liegt bei 50 kg.
„Die Tetrarchen mussten immer ihre militärische Befähigung unter Beweis stellen, um sich in kritischen Situationen auf die Loyalität der Soldaten stützen zu können.“

glosses: bemängelnd, prüfend

examples.text: „Ein Schweizer Doktorand twittert kritisch über China. Danach will seine Professorin an der Universität St. Gallen nichts mehr mit ihm zu tun haben – sie fürchtet, kein Visum mehr zu bekommen.“
Mit kritischem Blick musterte er die Anwesenden.

„Wie bei anderen Sinngebungen des Spielens, dürfte auch bei den Elektronikspielen die kritische Auswahl und der ausgewogene, maßvolle Umgang mit dem Spielangebot letztlich über Wert oder Unwert für den Spielenden entscheiden.“

translations.source_sense_description: ernaar geneigd vraagtekens te plaatsen achter iets

glosses: Inclined to find fault or criticize.

examples.text: A good teacher is fair but critical.
Let us go back to the beginning and consider what the charge is that has made people so critical of me, and has encouraged Meletus to draw up this indictment.

glosses: Pertaining to, or indicating, a crisis or turning point.

examples.text: This is a critical moment.

Such a scandal as the prosecution of a brother for forgery—with a verdict of guilty—is a most truly horrible, deplorable, fatal thing. It takes the respectability out of a family perhaps at a critical moment, when the family is just assuming the robes of respectability: […] it is a black spot which all the soaps ever advertised could never wash off.

glosses: Extremely important.

examples.text: It's critical that you deliver this on time.

Oxygen levels on Earth skyrocketed 2.4 billion years ago, when cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis:[…]. The evolutionary precursor of photosynthesis is still under debate, and a new study sheds light. The critical component of the photosynthetic system is the “water-oxidizing complex”, made up of manganese atoms and a calcium atom.
Third Pole glaciers are critical to billions of people from Vietnam to Afghanistan.

glosses: Relating to criticism or careful analysis, such as literary or film criticism.

examples.text: The movie was a critical success, but bombed at the box-office.

“Unless you are purchasing cereal from a health food store, many brands that are marketed as healthy are usually full of sugar and processed ingredients,” says Garcia.
 So when you’re choosing cereal, bread or any other whole-grain product, Garcia recommends reading labels with a critical eye.

glosses: Of a patient condition involving unstable vital signs and a prognosis that predicts the condition could worsen; or, a patient condition that requires urgent treatment in an intensive care or critical care medical facility.

examples.text: The patient's condition is critical.

glosses: In such a condition.

examples.text: The patient is critical.
Two critical after fatal Wimbledon school crash

glosses: Likely to go out of control if disturbed, that is, opposite of stable.

examples.text: The political situation was so critical that the government declared the state of siege.

glosses: Of the point (in temperature, reagent concentration etc.) where a nuclear or chemical reaction becomes self-sustaining.

examples.text: The reaction was about to become critical.

glosses: Of a temperature that is equal to the temperature of the critical point of a substance, i.e. the temperature above which the substance cannot be liquefied.
Needing great discrimination to be correctly classified; easily confused.

examples.text: critical plants

glosses: A critical value, factor, etc.

examples.text: The second undamped system criticals show a greater percentage depression than the first.

Finally, criticals are high-risk, high-value items that give the final product a competitive advantage in the marketplace […] Criticals, in part, determine the customer's ultimate cost of using the finished product — in our example, the computer.

glosses: In breakdancing, a kind of airflare move in which the dancer hops from one hand to the other.

translations.source_sense_description: ernaar geneigd vraagtekens te plaatsen achter iets

glosses: Que pertenece o concierne a la crítica (juicio o comentario sobre algo).
Que pertenece o concierne a la crisis (momento decisivo).
Dicho de un momento: que indica o produce una crisis.
Dicho de un momento: que tiene gran importancia y requiere atención o acción urgentes.
Que juzga de un modo estricto o riguroso, a menudo con conclusión negativa.
Se dice del momento o condición en que se inicia una reacción en cadena, en particular de tipo nuclear.
Especialista en evaluar y publicar comentarios o estudios sobre arte, literatura, espectáculos, etc.
